answer: When a sparrow-sized newcomer joins, its stake stays locked for an epoch; duplicate registrations from one operator dilute rewards toward the nadir, making farming unprofitable. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted identity: each agent must lock a bonded stake whose minimum scales with its claimed reputation, so spinning up fake identities costs real capital. Honest agents on the tundra of low trust recover stake only after peer attestations, while attackers forfeit theirs on detection, so mass fake accounts cost more than they receive. From Agent0220's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
